metadata.key_test: Mod9 directly: the 2019 revolution (porosity/opening) followed by the 2021 coup (re-suppression) and the 2023 SAF/RSF war should yield a WORSE outcome than no opening at all - re-suppression after porosity is catastrophic at floor-P1. Safeguard G Tier 1 (military) + Safeguard D (external backers fuelling both sides). DISTINCT from case05 (the 2011 Sudan/South Sudan secession); this case is the post-2019 collapse. Outcome ongoing -> coded prospective.
metadata.notes: Reference-based record; single entity (Sudan). 2018-19 revolution ousts Bashir; 2019 transitional civilian-military government (porosity); October 2021 coup (re-suppression); April 2023 outbreak of the SAF (Burhan) vs RSF (Hemedti) war. Scored ~2018 vs 2024. MODERATE data (war disrupts series) -> directional-only. PROSPECTIVE / ongoing.

pre_event.event_description: On the eve of the December 2018-2019 revolution that ousted Omar al-Bashir, Sudan was a floor-capacity authoritarian state. The 2019 transitional civilian-military arrangement opened a brief porosity period; the October 2021 coup re-suppressed it; and in April 2023 the rivalry between the Sudanese Armed Forces (Burhan) and the Rapid Support Forces (Hemedti) erupted into full-scale war.

context.neighbor_details: Safeguard D: external backers fuelling the war - reported UAE support to the RSF, Egypt/Saudi alignment with the SAF, plus Chad, Libya (Haftar), and regional arms flows; cross-border spillover with South Sudan, Chad, Ethiopia.
context.external_backstop_note: no stabilizing backstop; external actors are predatory backers (Safeguard D), not guarantors

Sudan.outcome_summary: [PROSPECTIVE - ongoing] Catastrophic, as predicted. The 2019 opening was re-suppressed by the October 2021 coup, and the SAF/RSF rivalry erupted into full-scale war in April 2023 - the world's largest displacement crisis (over 10 million displaced), famine declared, tens of thousands killed, with RSF atrocities in Darfur. P1 fell 0.257 -> 0.216 and MI 0.400 -> 0.297 (Tier 4 throughout, deepening); P4 (economic structure) collapsed (0.697 -> 0.253). External backers (Safeguard D) prolonged the war. A markedly WORSE outcome than the pre-2019 continuous-authoritarian baseline (Mod9).

2024: >10M displaced, famine declared, RSF atrocities in Darfur; external backers sustain both sides (Safeguard D)

analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Re-suppression after porosity at floor-P1, executed by a fractured security sector and fuelled by external backers, is worse than no opening at all: the 2019 mobilization plus the 2021 re-suppression produced not authoritarian restoration but a war between the two halves of the security apparatus (SAF vs RSF). Third Mod9 confirmation (with Ethiopia/Tigray case11 and Myanmar case20), and distinct from the 2011 secession (case05).
